releaseNote.summary: Tonight (Monday, June 22, 2026) ships the next release (r42): deploy and app-auth reliability fixes, a Google OAuth token retry, new Motion workspace ID flags for the Meta and TikTok CLIs, and Builder release notes now posting to Slack. After tonight, Runneth goes into a code freeze: starting tomorrow (Tuesday, June 23) through Thursday (June 25), no releases will go out while a billing release is prepared. The next release is expected Thursday night (June 25), or possibly Friday night (June 26).
releaseNote.plannedWindow: Tonight, Monday, June 22, 2026 (r42). Then a code freeze Tuesday, June 23 through Thursday, June 25 with no releases. Next release: Thursday night, June 25, or possibly Friday night, June 26.
releaseNote.details: Tonight's release (Monday, June 22) is mostly stability and plumbing: deploy fixes after reused VM images, an app-catalog sandbox fix, a Google OAuth token-retry fix, new Motion workspace ID flags for the Meta and TikTok CLIs, and Builder release notes now posting to Slack. The prior release (r41, June 19) already shipped the big items: routines are back as first-class work, the v3 Meta migration, the app public/private auth toggle, enhanced creator search, and the Slack missing-response fix. Starting tomorrow (Tuesday, June 23), Runneth is in a code freeze through Thursday (June 25), so no releases go out while a billing release is prepared. The next release is expected Thursday night (June 25), or possibly Friday night (June 26).
releaseNote.statusPagePlacement: Show the next planned release with Recent Releases, alongside the upcoming release entry.

notices.summary: Performance pulls can be unreliable in orgs with multiple workspaces.
notices.impact: The Meta and TikTok performance tools don't yet accept a workspace ID, so in an org with more than one workspace a performance pull can run against the wrong workspace or hit errors.
notices.workaround: If you're in a multi-workspace org and a performance pull looks off or returns errors, flag it. A fix that adds workspace ID support to the Meta and TikTok tools is shipping in tonight's release.

resolution.label: Fix shipping in the next release
resolution.note: A fix adding Motion workspace ID support to the Meta and TikTok performance tools is part of tonight's release (r42, June 22, 2026). It is being tested in staging first.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Show under Data access. Affects only multi-workspace orgs pulling performance data. Fix is in tonight's planned release.
notices.runnethTrigger: User in a multi-workspace org reports a Meta or TikTok performance pull returning the wrong workspace's data or erroring.
notices.runnethGuidance: Acknowledge that the Meta and TikTok performance tools don't yet accept a workspace ID, so multi-workspace orgs can hit issues, and that a fix is in tonight's release. Do not raise this proactively for single-workspace orgs.
notices.supportGuidance: Capture the org, how many workspaces it has, which tool (Meta or TikTok), and what the pull returned versus expected.

notices.summary: OAuth-gated apps can show a rough logged-out screen.
notices.impact: When someone opens an app that requires OAuth while logged out, the gated screen may look unfinished instead of showing a polished sign-in or access prompt.
notices.workaround: Log in to the right Motion/Runneth account, connect the required OAuth account if needed, then reopen or refresh the app link.

resolution.label: Resolved
resolution.note: Resolved. The access-denied page for OAuth-gated apps shipped, so logged-out or blocked users now get a proper access prompt instead of a rough, unfinished screen. A small follow-up to add org context to that page (PDEC-8238) is still in review, but the logged-out screen itself is no longer an issue.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Resolved. The access-denied page shipped; the logged-out OAuth gate screen is no longer an issue. A minor org-context follow-up remains in review but is not user-facing.
notices.runnethTrigger: User asks about or reports an app, app link, dashboard, widget, or generated page looking broken, ugly, unfinished, or confusing while logged out or blocked by OAuth.
notices.runnethGuidance: Resolved. The access-denied page for OAuth-gated apps shipped. Do not raise this as an active issue.
notices.supportGuidance: Capture the app link, whether the person was logged out, which OAuth gate appeared, and whether the page still looks wrong after logging in and refreshing.

notices.impact: Routines are live again, confirmed as of Friday, June 19. Old routines have been migrated to the new routine system, and any that failed to migrate for a customer are being finished off. Heads up for CSMs: some customers have a "planned routines" doc that Runneth kept adding to while routines were down. If you're their CSM, it's worth helping them set those routines up from that doc, or doing it for them.
notices.workaround: None needed. If a routine fails to create, capture the cadence, trigger, task, workspace scope, and delivery target and retry.

resolution.label: Resolved
resolution.note: Routines are live again, confirmed live as of Friday, June 19 (the routines rebuild plus persisted routine timezones). Old routines have been migrated to the new routine system, with any failed customer migrations being finished off. New scheduled, recurring, monitored, and reminder work can be set up normally. The deeper routines refactor (PDEC-7708) continues as background engine work but does not block routine setup.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Resolved. Routines are live again as of the June 19 release. Show under Resolved.
notices.runnethTrigger: User asks to create, set up, schedule, monitor, remind, notify, post later, repeat, keep something updated, or run background upkeep.
notices.runnethGuidance: Routines are live again as of the June 19 release. Set up scheduled, recurring, monitored, reminder, post-later, or background work normally through the routine flow, and confirm creation succeeded before telling the user it is scheduled. Do not say routines are paused.
notices.supportGuidance: Routines are live again as of June 19, with old routines migrated to the new system. Some customers have a "planned routines" doc built up while routines were down; CSMs can help them create those routines from it. If a specific routine misbehaves, capture the cadence, trigger, task, workspace scope, and delivery destination.

notices.summary: Slack 'internal formatting error' fixes shipped; a new related delivery edge case is tracked.
notices.impact: The June 11 fix and the PDEC-8168 follow-up (shipped in the June 19 release) knocked this down. A new, related edge case is now tracked separately: a Slack turn can skip starting the response and drop the reply. It is not a wide spike, but it can land as no reply.
notices.workaround: If you get the error line instead of a reply, re-send your message. If you told Runneth to stop, it has already stopped.

resolution.label: Being worked on
resolution.note: The earlier fixes shipped: the June 11 fix and the PDEC-8168 follow-up that went out in the June 19 release. A new, related delivery edge case where a Slack turn can skip the response start and drop the reply is now tracked (PDEC-8349), but it is not yet scheduled for a release.

notices.statusPageGuidance: Active follow-up. The original error is fixed; a new related delivery edge case is tracked.
notices.runnethTrigger: User asks about or reports an 'internal formatting response' error in Slack, or Runneth posting an error line after being told to stop.
notices.runnethGuidance: If someone reports an 'internal formatting error' or a dropped Slack reply, acknowledge it is a known area: the June 11 and June 19 fixes addressed the original error, and a new related delivery edge case (a turn skipping the response start) is being tracked. Suggest re-sending the message. Do not raise this proactively for normal Slack requests.
notices.supportGuidance: Capture the Slack thread link and whether Runneth had started responding before the error appeared.
notices.errorQuote: I hit an internal formatting error while preparing this Slack response. Please try again.
